questions.q: What did Yahweh say was happening on the exact day he spoke to Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem on that exact day.

questions.q: In Yahweh’s parable, what does Yahweh tell the people of Jerusalem to do?
questions.a: Yahweh tells them to pour water into the cooking pot, fill it with the best bones, and boil it thoroughly.

questions.q: What is wrong with the cooking pot of Jerusalem that will not come out of it?
questions.a: The cooking pot of Jerusalem has rust in it that will not come out of it.

questions.q: What has Jerusalem done to exact vengeance from Yahweh?
questions.a: Jerusalem has not covered the blood that is in her midst.

questions.q: Why set the empty pot on the fire?
questions.a: Set the empty pot on the fire in order to heat and scorch its bronze, so its uncleanness within it will be melted, its corrosion consumed!

questions.q: What has not been removed from Jerusalem by the fire?
questions.a: The corrosion of Jerusalem has not been removed by the fire.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, by what will the people of Jerusalem be judged?
questions.a: The people of Jerusalem will be judged by their ways and their activities.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he was taking from Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he was taking Ezekiel’s wife from him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel not to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel not to mourn or weep for having lost his wife.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say was the meaning of the events which happened to Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the desire of the people’s eyes was defiling the sanctuary, so their sons and daughters would fall by the sword.

questions.q: What would the people of Jerusalem do when they suffered their loss?
questions.a: The people would do exactly as Ezekiel did, and not mourn or weep.

questions.q: As what did Ezekiel serve for the people of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Ezekiel served as a sign for the people of Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen on the day the temple was captured?
questions.a: Yahweh said that on the day the temple was captured, a refugee would come to Ezekiel to give him the news.

questions.q: On the day the temple was captured, what would the people of Jerusalem know?
questions.a: On the day the temple was captured, the people of Jerusalem would know that the Lord is Yahweh.

commentary.text: The fate of Jerusalem. (Ezek. 24:1-14) The extent of the sufferings of the Jews. (Ezek. 24:15-27)

Ezek. 24:1-14 The pot on the fire represented Jerusalem besieged by the Chaldeans: all orders and ranks were within the walls, prepared as a prey for the enemy. They ought to have put away their transgressions, as the scum, which rises by the heat of the fire, is taken from the top of the pot. But they grew worse, and their miseries increased. Jerusalem was to be levelled with the ground. The time appointed for the punishment of wicked men may seem to come slowly, but it will come surely. It is sad to think how many there are, on whom ordinances and providences are all lost.

Ezek. 24:15-27 Though mourning for the dead is a duty, yet it must be kept under by religion and right reason: we must not sorrow as men that have no hope. Believers must not copy the language and expressions of those who know not God. The people asked the meaning of the sign. God takes from them all that was dearest to them. And as Ezekiel wept not for his affliction, so neither should they weep for theirs. Blessed be God, we need not pine away under our afflictions; for should all comforts fail, and all sorrows be united, yet the broken heart and the mourner's prayer are always acceptable before God.
